security_audit.summary: The skill is useful, but it repeatedly recommends piping a remote installer directly into a shell, which is a critical community-skill supply-chain risk. Most Markdown command examples are false positives, while local file uploads and X automation create real data exposure and account-action risks.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell instructions with separate download, inspection, signature verification, and execution steps.

remediation.issue: Manual installation builds a download command from a remote manifest.
remediation.suggestion: Provide pinned release URLs, published checksums, and signature verification before extraction or installation.

remediation.issue: Local file paths are automatically uploaded to cloud apps.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation for each local path and warn users before uploading parent-directory or home-directory files.

remediation.issue: X automation can mutate a social account.
remediation.suggestion: Require clear human approval before posting, sending messages, following users, liking posts, or retweeting.

remediation.issue: API key guidance may lead users to expose credentials in shared shells or logs.
remediation.suggestion: Explain secret handling practices and warn users not to paste real keys into prompts, logs, or public files.

content.user_title: Run AI Apps with inference.sh CLI
content.value_statement: Teams need a consistent way to run cloud AI apps without custom API setup. This skill guides inference.sh CLI discovery, execution, authentication, and task tracking.
actual_capabilities: Guides installation, login, updates, and API key setup for the belt CLI.
Shows how to list, search, filter, and inspect inference.sh apps.
Provides examples for image, video, LLM, search, 3D, and X apps.
Explains inline input, input files, version pinning, and no-wait task submission.
Covers local file uploads and task result retrieval for generated media.
limitations: Requires the external inference.sh service and a valid account.
The CLI may upload local files when paths are used as inputs.
It does not verify app safety, costs, quotas, or output licensing.
Some examples require third-party app credentials or platform permissions.

use_cases.title: Prototype media generation
use_cases.description: Find and run image, video, audio, and 3D apps from a single CLI workflow.

use_cases.title: Compare AI model apps
use_cases.description: Search app catalogs, inspect schemas, create sample inputs, and track repeatable test runs.

use_cases.title: Operate cloud AI tasks
use_cases.description: Submit long-running jobs, retrieve task results, and manage outputs from command-line sessions.

prompt_templates.title: Find an app
prompt_templates.prompt: Use infsh-cli to find image generation apps and explain the safest next step before running one.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a run
prompt_templates.prompt: Use infsh-cli to create a sample input for falai/flux-dev-lora, then wait for my review before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Track a long task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use infsh-cli to submit google/veo-3-1-fast without waiting, then show how to check status and save results.

prompt_templates.title: Design a guarded workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use infsh-cli to plan a workflow that searches apps, reviews schemas, confirms file uploads, runs selected jobs, and records task IDs.

output_examples.input: Find a fast image generation app for a product mockup.
output_examples.output: Suggested app: falai/flux-2-klein-lora. Next step: inspect the app schema, prepare a sample input, and confirm any local file upload.

output_examples.input: Run a long video generation job and let me check it later.
output_examples.output: Recommended flow: submit the job without waiting, record the task ID, then check status and save the final result when ready.

output_examples.input: Help me use a local image in a cloud upscaler.
output_examples.output: Recommended flow: confirm the exact file path, verify the app input schema, run the upscaler, and retrieve the generated media URL.

best_practices: Inspect an app schema before running it with production inputs.
Confirm every local file path before allowing uploads to inference.sh.
Use version pinning and task IDs for repeatable long-running jobs.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installers into a shell without reviewing the script.
Do not pass secrets or private files into third-party apps without approval.
Do not automate X posting, follows, or messages without explicit human confirmation.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use the inference.sh CLI to find and run cloud AI apps.

faq.question: Do I need an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. Most commands require the belt CLI, authentication, and available account quota.

faq.question: Can it run Claude models?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes OpenRouter examples for Claude and other language models.

faq.question: Can it upload local files?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI uploads local paths for app inputs, so confirm every path before use.

faq.question: Is the installer risk-free?
faq.answer: No. The skill recommends curl-to-shell installation, which should be replaced with verified manual steps.

faq.question: How are long-running jobs handled?
faq.answer: The skill explains no-wait submission, task status checks, and saving task results.
